items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: He'd come and he took two, three lessons. With me at five or twelve dolphins in the street.

ctx.x: It's by the… Yeah. The music. The count of the lives.

The division. If you know the lives, you can't play. Some of them know the music though. They get up there, they play, they play, but when you come to a club, you play with somebody else you don't know why you're at. It's just as bad. Well I tried to show them. Johnny Lindsay, he was playing with the rubber shows. He's in the, Johnny Lindsay plays trombone. And he was playing at the larynx thing. And I was living right there at that chord. See that chord you've got there, five or twelve dolphins. Oh yeah, yeah.…

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: So, he asked me, he said, tell him I want to take a couple of lessons.

ctx.x: Johnny. I heard him on bass. I never heard him on trombone.

You heard him on bass? Yeah, in Chicago. He used to play with, uh, what he used to play with? A robot show. Well, he used to play at a robot show. Well, he used to play at a robot show. I'm trying more. So, he was playing at the palace. He was playing at the palace and, uh, so he, he was a good reader. But he wasn't sure. You understand? Yeah. Yeah. So, he asked me, he said, tell him I want to take a couple of lessons. I live at 512 Dolphin Street. So, I say, yes, come on. But he could play and I was getting that…
